title: Keep the review flag off the ledger export

blocks.text: The accounting team reviews large journal entries on a screen that flags every amount at or above a limit with `[review]`. At month end the same entries go out as a CSV file, and the import on the other side rejects any amount column that isn't a plain number. Each exported entry id also carries the accounting period after it, so `AP-9` in March 2031 becomes `AP-9/2031-03`.
`Ledger.PlainFormat` and `Ledger.FlaggedFormat` already render amounts. Finish the three `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/Ledger.java`, each of which returns a function that other code calls later:

items: `withPeriod(String period)`: the function the export applies to each entry id;
`FlaggedFormat.exportColumn()`: the function for the export's amount column;
`FlaggedFormat.screenColumn()`: the function for the review screen. Teams extend `FlaggedFormat` to restyle their own screen, and the screen must show their style.

blocks.text: One line each, about three lines in total. A method reference fits some of them; whether it fits each one is part of the task.

cases.says: an exported entry id holds the original id and the period, and nothing else
the export column and the screen column both show the amount in units and two decimals
the period is written after the entry id, not in front of it
the export column shows the plain amount, without the review flag, even for amounts above the limit
the screen column renders through the object's own format, so a format that extends the flagged one changes what the screen shows

origin.section: A Bound Reference Holds Its Receiver, and the Interface's Arguments Become the Method's

concepts: A bound reference fixes its receiver, so every interface argument goes to the method: suffix::concat puts the suffix in front, and the value-as-receiver form needs a lambda.
this::m dispatches to the object's override, while super::m always runs the parent's body.
